## The tank called Cushing

Cushing is a small city in Oklahoma.
Several pipelines meet there, and it is the point where the West Texas Intermediate futures traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange are physically delivered.

How much oil is left in that city's tanks is what sets the benchmark price of US oil.
Oil can pile up somewhere else in the country, but if the tanks at the delivery point drain, the futures price follows the delivery point.

A tank cannot be emptied all the way.

A volume the pumps cannot lift has to stay at the bottom, and stocks cannot go below it.
The Energy Information Administration said that between June 19 and July 10 Cushing stocks fell under 20 million barrels and approached that limit.
Stocks have recovered a little since, but the place that sets the price is still sitting near that line.

## How inventory turns into price

A national inventory average does not show the last box on this path.

@@REF@@Oil Market Report, August 2026 (International Energy Agency, 2026-08-12)|https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-august-2026|https://iea.imgix.net/9e69d31f-3789-4cdd-8a28-e020e81380cf/08-August.jpg?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&h=600&q=80&rect=488%2C0%2C1200%2C1200&w=1200

The International Energy Agency wrote that observed global oil stocks fell below 7.9 billion barrels at the end of July.
Some 410 million barrels have drained since the war began, and the agency put the third-quarter shortfall at 1.8 million barrels a day.
The same report sees global supply falling by 4.3 million barrels a day in 2026 and rebounding by 8.3 million next year to 110.3 million barrels a day. That rebound appears to assume the current disruptions unwind.

## The two months Hanke staked

If national stocks are average while the delivery point is draining, the open question is which number is setting the price right now.
What can be graded in Hanke's sentence is the price.

He said oil comes roaring back within two months.
Brent stood at $93.60 a barrel on August 19, already 41% above where it was a year earlier.
For it to climb from here, the news has to come out of Hormuz.
The force that would lift the price sits in transit counts more than in inventory statistics, which makes this closer to a forecast about the war than about oil.

SEMI certification is an international industry standard that judges whether a piece of semiconductor equipment is safe for the people and the plant around it.
It is paperwork that has to be in hand before a tool can be loaded onto a ship and sent to another country, and without it the tool does not clear the port.

That puts the certification at the very front of the queue when a fab is being built.
It is the kind of step that is already too late if you get to it after the building is up.

What stands out here is the order.

Samsung has run its returns in three-year programmes.

All three together come to 102.5 trillion won.

## What separates a dividend from a cancellation

There are two ways to hand money back.
A cash dividend moves money from the company's account to the shareholder's account.
A share cancellation has the company buy its own stock and destroy it, so fewer shares remain and each surviving share owns more.

The difference that matters here is the ownership percentage.
When the share count falls, a holder who kept the same number of shares sees their percentage rise on its own.

A day earlier, on August 19, SK hynix said it would buy back and cancel 40 trillion won of its own stock, some 24.07 million shares, or about 3.3% of those outstanding.

@@REF@@SK hynix launches record $29b share buyback and cancellation after stock loses half its value (Korea JoongAng Daily, 2026-08-19)|https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/sk-hynix-launches-record-29b-share-buyback-and-cancellation-after-stock-loses-half-its-value/12832819

SK hynix's largest shareholder is SK Square, which holds 20.1%.
Korean fair trade law requires a company under a holding structure to keep at least 20% of a listed subsidiary.
That 20.1% leaves a tenth of a percentage point of room.

Cancellation works in the direction of widening that room.
Samsung has no such percentage constraint, which is why the original post reads dividends as the easier instrument for its governance structure.

## The price of tripling the payout

A company that does not return it now will have nothing to return in the downturn.|The case for holding|The same cash is what pays for the US fabs and the next process node. The split is whether the same cash is money to spend now or money already spoken for.

First-half capital spending ran 28 trillion won, which points to roughly 60 trillion for the year.
On the foundry side the second Taylor fab in Texas is set to break ground at year-end, and on the memory side the Pyeongtaek lines keep expanding.
This payout shares an account with those plans.

There is a policy backdrop as well.
Korea moved dividend income tax to a progressive schedule in January, from 14% below 20 million won to 30% above 5 billion won.
Larger dividends therefore carry a tax bill for controlling shareholders, so choosing dividends anyway says the governance reason outweighs the tax one.

A 9% move on an unconfirmed number means the board resolution either confirms the expectation or trims it.
If the total clears 100 trillion won with a special dividend inside it, the reporting was right. If it lands below that, or if no resolution comes in August, the market ran ahead.
After that, watch the mix. How that total splits between dividends and cancellations shows whether this company is returning cash for reasons that sit in the ownership register or in the cash flow statement.

On the same date a year earlier, 49 did.

Hormuz is the only way out of the Persian Gulf.
Crude lifted by Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait and Iran all leaves through that one narrow lane.
Since the blockade that began in late February 2026, traffic through it has served as a direct gauge of world oil supply.

@@REF@@Hormuz Tanker Traffic Slows to a Trickle (OilPrice, 2026-08-17)|https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/Hormuz-Tanker-Traffic-Slows-to-a-Trickle.html|https://d32r1sh890xpii.cloudfront.net/news/1200x675/2026-08-17_cetv58ho2j.jpg

Brent was in the $88 range over the same stretch.

@@SHARE@@The corridor Iran drew|about 90%|90|The Omani lane|about 10%|10@@During the truce in early June the split was 60 to 40. As the traffic itself thinned out, the ships that remained crowded into the lane Iran set.@@Kpler 2026-07-23 · for the week of July 15 to 22, 2026

## From 45 a day to 13

June 7 to July 7 was a truce.
Daily crossings averaged 45 over that stretch.
After fighting resumed on July 7, the average fell to 13 a day.

A drop of 70%.

That number does not only mean less crude is moving.
When ships thin out, the freight and insurance costs on the ones still sailing go up, and that cost is added to the price of oil.
Put simply, it is not the goods that got more expensive but the carrying of them, and what reaches the consumer is the same either way.

## The lane Iran drew

In April, Iran declared a transit corridor hugging its own coastline.
The International Maritime Organization has never approved it, and neither the United States nor the European Union recognizes it.

During the truce, 60% of traffic used that lane and 40% used the Omani side.
By mid-July the split was 90 to 10, and on the last day Kpler tallied, every vessel that crossed used the Iranian lane.
Separately from which navy patrols the strait, what shows up here is which channel the ships actually choose.

@@CMP@@The count that says it reopened|Transits resumed after the June 17 memorandum, and June 24 saw 54 in a single day, the most since the conflict began.|The count Hanke is running|Before the war, 138 vessels a day went through. Even the best day, 54, is under 40% of that, and August 18 was 4.

One side counts what has come back and the other counts what has not, from the same transit tallies. It splits on whether the baseline sits in June or before the war.

@@REF@@Iran Shipping Update (United Against Nuclear Iran, 2026-08-18)|https://www.unitedagainstnucleariran.com/analysis/iran-shipping-update-august-18-2026

On the strength of those numbers Hanke wrote that the claim that the United States controls the strait does not hold, and that Iran does.

## What August 18 leaves behind

There are two things to watch rather than one: the count of transits and the split between the lanes.
If daily crossings climb back toward the 40s and the Omani share rises with them, operating control of the strait has returned to where it was; if only the count rises while traffic stays crowded into the Iranian lane, the volume recovers but the terms of passage stay Iran's to set.
In the second case oil flows, and the risk premium attached to that flow does not go away.

What sets the price right now is not how much crude sits under the Gulf but how many ships cross the water above it.

serenity-optical-shortage-elaser-sold-ou:
The optical parts that carry data between chips inside an AI data center are going to be short for years, and this quarter three suppliers said so in a row.
Applied Optoelectronics posted revenue of $191.9 million for April through June, up 86% from a year earlier, and founder and chief executive Thompson Lin said demand will keep outrunning the company's production capacity through the middle of 2027.

@@REF@@Applied Optoelectronics reports second quarter 2026 results (company release, 2026-08-06)|https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/06/3340777/9986/en/applied-optoelectronics-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html

In the same month Lumentum reported $1.01 billion for the quarter that ended in late June, more than double the year-earlier figure.
MACOM said the orders it took in that quarter ran to 1.6 times what it shipped.

## What the optical part actually does

To use tens of thousands of graphics processors inside a data center as if they were one machine, they have to talk to each other without pause.
Copper smears the signal as soon as the distance grows.
So the electrical signal is turned into light, sent down a glass fiber, and turned back into electricity at the far end.

The finger-sized part that does that conversion is an optical transceiver.
It sits where the connector on an office network cable sits, except there is a laser inside it.

Above 800 gigabits per second, that laser is not built on silicon. It is built on a different semiconductor substrate called indium phosphide.
Indium phosphide emits light directly when current runs through it and silicon does not, so the laser has nowhere else to sit.
Only a handful of plants in the world work with the material.

## The ramp is already threefold

@@BAR@@Capacity today, per month|200,000 units|20|Year-end target, per month|650,000 units|65@@This is the rate at which Applied Optoelectronics builds 800G and 1.6T optical modules. The plan is to triple it with four months to go, and the company still says that will not meet demand.@@Company second-quarter 2026 results, 2026-08-06

More than one supplier is promising a ramp like this.
The problem sits one step upstream.

## The blockage is in front of the laser

Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston said in late July that indium phosphide supply is running more than 30% below what customers are asking for, and that the gap is wider than anything seen in DRAM or NAND.

@@REF@@Lumentum CEO warns of a bottleneck in a critical silicon photonics material (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-31)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/lumentum-ceo-says-the-indium-phosphide-shortage-will-become-worse-than-memory|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ibEpXbFzhNegj42rkqPzgZ-1920-80.jpg

Tom's Hardware reports the shortfall is stuck in two places at once, at the fabs and in the raw material.
A module maker can triple its assembly lines, and if the lasers to fill them do not arrive at the same rate the lines run empty.

This is where the comparison with memory stops being tidy.
Memory adds output by pushing more wafers through the same fab. Optical modules need the substrate itself before anything else.

## What was said in Taiwan on August 18

@@TIME@@April 20, 2026|TrendForce forecasts the AI optical transceiver market at $26 billion for 2026, up 57%, naming component shortages as the main constraint|July 31, 2026|Lumentum says the material shortage is worse than memory|August 6, 2026|Applied Optoelectronics says supply will trail demand through the middle of 2027|August 18, 2026|eLaser general manager Song Tian-Zeng says the entire supply chain is out of stock|>Early November 2026|Applied Optoelectronics third-quarter results@@In four months the same message came down the chain in order: forecast, material, module, packaging. That makes it more than one company's problem.@@TrendForce 2026-04-20; Tom's Hardware 2026-07-31; company release 2026-08-06; DigiTimes 2026-08-19

eLaser, listed in Taipei, packages laser diodes into chip form.
At its August 18 investor conference general manager Song Tian-Zeng said the keyword for AI optical communications over the next few years is one word, shortage.
Printed circuit boards, the carrier boards that chips sit on, laser chips, packaging capacity: almost everything attached to the AI chain is short, he said.

The original post lays the memory supercycle over that remark.
For the overlay to hold, two things have to match. Demand has to be visible years out, and adding supply has to take years.
Order books already speak to the first. The second is set by how long it takes to build substrate capacity.

That makes Applied Optoelectronics' third-quarter revenue, due in early November, the place this splits.
Landing inside the $255 million to $290 million range the company guided to means the new lines actually ran. Coming in under it means the lines were added and the lasers to fill them were not found.
The phase where a shortage raises prices and the phase where a shortage cuts revenue come out of the same shortage.

It crossed $39 trillion in March of this year, and $38 trillion in October of last year.

## A trillion every five months

A total on its own does not land.
Debt is felt first as the interest that goes out every month, not as the principal.
Buying a house works the same way: the monthly payment, not the loan size, sets how you live.

A government is no different.
The $40 trillion is not a sum to be repaid so much as a sum to be reborrowed at whatever rate prevails when each piece matures.
So what sets the budget is less the size of the pile than the rate attached to it.
With long-term yields rising, the same $40 trillion gets more expensive every year.
The more of it matures soon, the faster that repricing shows up.

The route by which debt squeezes a budget runs through this line, not through the headline total.@@Checked 2026-08-20 · Treasury debt total and interest figures as reported by NPR, 2026-08-19

## The line that crowds out the others

Interest payments now run above $1 trillion a year.
Lined up against other spending, they sit behind Social Security and ahead of defense.
Interest in the first ten months of fiscal 2026 was 15% higher than in the same stretch a year earlier.

Margaret Spellings, who leads the Bipartisan Policy Center, said the federal debt is already raising the cost of living and choking out other spending and investment.
Crowding out is not a metaphor here but a line in the budget. The money available in a year is fixed, and interest is not a line that politics sets. It is a line that contracts set.

## The two things that happened on August 19

On the same day the $40 trillion figure landed, the Treasury doubled its long-bond buybacks from $2 billion per operation to at least $4 billion.
A buyback is the government purchasing its own long-dated bonds back from the market to press long-term yields down.
The cash for it comes from newly issued debt.

That is where it splits.
If the new issuance is concentrated in short maturities, a larger share of the $40 trillion reprices within a year; if the long-dated share of issuance holds, the total grows while the maturity profile stays put.

What it actually bought that day was $1 billion of a bond maturing in 2048 and $1 billion spread across two 2051s.
The cap went up at the exact spot where sellers outnumbered the buyer ten to one.

## A buyback is not a repayment

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing back old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for it comes from selling new debt.
Nothing is retired on net. Only the maturity mix moves.

@@FLOW@@Issue bills|Sell new three-month paper to raise cash|Run the operation|Buy old long bonds back from dealers|Shrink the long end|Fewer long bonds circulate, so their price rises and their yield falls@@The path starts and ends at different maturities. Every long bond taken out is replaced by short paper that has to be borrowed again within months.

Long yields do fall along this path.
What remains open is where the cost of that lands.

## Buying 1.9% while issuing at 3.7%

Wolf Street took apart one of the securities bought in this operation.
It is a 30-year bond issued in February 2021, maturing in February 2051, carrying a coupon of 1.9%.
The Treasury bought it at 52.375 cents on the dollar.
That turned $334 million of face value into roughly $175 million of cash paid.

@@REF@@Bessent doubles the buybacks, swapping old cheap debt at a discount for new expensive debt (Wolf Street, 2026-08-19)|https://wolfstreet.com/2026/08/19/bessent-doubles-yellens-hocus-pocus-treasury-buybacks-swapping-old-cheap-debt-at-a-discount-for-new-expensive-debt/

But the old bond that disappeared cost $6.3 million a year to service, while the bills issued to fund the purchase cost about $7.0 million a year.
The debt shrank and the annual interest bill grew.

@@CHK@@Three-month bill rate|3.7%|Coupon on the bond bought|1.9%|30-year market yield|5.3%@@The coupon on the retired bond was fixed in the era of cheap money, while the short paper taking its place is priced at today's cost. The coupon is CUSIP 912810SU3 as verified by Wolf Street.

The shortening of maturity comes with it.
Three-month paper matures four times a year, and each time it has to be borrowed again at whatever the rate is that day.
While rates sit where they are, that rollover passes quietly. Every rollover is also a repricing.

## What November 4 settles

The increase runs only from the September 9 operation through November 4.
Across seven operations in that window, the extra amount comes to $14 billion.
Against roughly $10 trillion of Treasuries outstanding in the 10-to-30-year sector, that addition is about a tenth of a percent.

So the force of this move is in the sentence rather than the sum.
It told anyone about to dump long bonds in a hurry that somebody is standing there to take them.

If the November 4 quarterly refunding keeps the larger size or raises it again, the interpretation the market bought in August was right.

The award covers six vehicles for $100.3 million, and rises to eighteen vehicles if the Army exercises every option.

@@REF@@South Korea's highly mobile 155mm artillery system wins US Army howitzer contract (The War Zone, 2026-08-18)|https://www.twz.com/land/south-koreas-highly-mobile-155mm-artillery-system-wins-u-s-army-howitzer-contract|https://www.twz.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/army-picks-k9mh-155mm-howitzer-for-prototyping-effort.jpg?w=1200

## What the units towing M777s are trying to fix

The M777 is a gun that a truck or a helicopter drags into position and sets down before it can fire.
Setting up takes time, and so does packing up and leaving.

On a battlefield covered by drones and counter-battery radar, the minutes a crew spends parked where it just fired are the minutes it is exposed.
Firing and immediately moving is what the Army calls shoot and scoot.
Hanwha says the K9MH takes under 30 seconds to emplace or displace.

Self-propelled artillery splits into tracked vehicles and wheeled ones.
Tracks spread the weight of the hull, so a tracked gun keeps moving through mud and up slopes, and it carries thicker armor.
The cost is weight and speed: moving one a long way usually means putting it on something else.

Wheels are the opposite trade.
A wheeled gun is lighter and faster, can drive hundreds of kilometers on its own, and fits inside a transport aircraft.
It pays for that with soft ground and thinner armor.

So the Army intends to leave tracked Paladins with its armored formations and give wheeled guns to the Stryker and infantry brigades that already move on wheels.
Hanwha's entry puts the automated turret of the in-service K9 onto an 8x8 wheeled chassis.

The memory etched into the wafer is SRAM.

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for those purchases comes from selling new bonds. The total stock of debt does not change; only its maturity mix does.

@@BAR@@Buybacks scheduled Aug to Nov|$75.2bn|752|Net issuance, prior quarter|$577bn|5770@@A buyback does not shrink what the Treasury is printing. ## Naming the price before you buy

Yield curve control means a central bank or a government pinning a chosen maturity below a set level.
It fixes the price first and then promises to take whatever volume shows up at that price.

Yields do come down when this works.

A refinery is where crude is boiled and separated into gasoline and diesel. When the plant stops, the crude does not vanish. It leaves the country as crude instead.

More crude looks for buyers and its price is held down, while less refined fuel is made and its price rises. Put simply, the wheat is still there and the mill has burned; what gets expensive is flour, not wheat. ## Buying and retiring are not the same

A buyback is a company purchasing its own stock in the market. Shares bought that way can sit in the corporate treasury, and from there they can be resold later, handed to employees as compensation, or swapped for a stake in another company. A buyback on its own therefore does not shrink the share count.

Cancellation erases those shares from the register.

Retired shares never come back, so the number of shares outstanding falls permanently, and the same profit is divided among fewer of them. That is also why Korean policymakers treat the two steps differently. Lawmakers have been debating an amendment to the Commercial Act that would require repurchased shares to be cancelled within a set period, because treasury stock parked indefinitely can protect a controlling shareholder's voting power instead of enlarging what minority holders own. The fact that this announcement is written as a cancellation rather than a purchase is the part that matters.

The test this card set on August 7 was whether the company could name a return figure while holding its expansion schedule. Half of that is now answered and half is not. meru-discount-rate-vs-thin-credit-spread:
The 30-year US Treasury yield has climbed to 5.3%, its highest level since 2007.
On the same day CoreWeave fell 8.3% and Fabrinet fell 10%,
while SK Hynix, SanDisk and Western Digital each dropped more than 5%.

@@REF@@Rising Yields, Oil Interrupt Rally, Hurting Chips (Charles Schwab, 2026-08-18)|https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/stock-market-update-open|https://www.schwab.com/sites/g/files/eyrktu1071/files/329122355_2x1.jpg

None of that means these companies will earn less money this year.
What shrank is the rate used to convert that money into today's value.

## Pushing 10 million won ten years out

The discount rate is the rate at which money you will receive later is marked down to what it is worth now.
Put simply, it is an interest rate turned around and run backwards.

Say you are due 10 million won a year from now.
At a 4% rate you only need to put 9.61 million won on deposit today to end up with 10 million,
so that future money is worth 9.61 million won today.
At 5% you need only 9.52 million won.
The same future sum just lost 90,000 won of present value.

Stretch the wait to ten years and the gap changes shape.
At 4% you need 6.76 million won today; at 5% you need 6.14 million.
The same one percentage point now costs 620,000 won, close to seven times the one-year figure.
Compounding does that: interest earns interest, and ten years of it piles up.

## Where banks and tech part ways

A bank that pays a steady dividend hands you money that behaves like one-year money.
The profits an AI company promises sit several years out.
So the same one percentage point moves the two share prices by very different amounts.

That is the first shock, and it arrives fast.
Nothing about the company's earnings changed. Only the price tag attached to those earnings did.

## When the spread is thin, the Treasury yield passes straight through

The second shock is slower.
Companies borrow at the Treasury yield plus a spread that reflects their own credit risk.
A wide spread absorbs part of a rise in Treasury yields. A thin one lets it through untouched.

That is the author's premise, so we went and looked the numbers up.

@@CHK@@30-year Treasury yield|5.31%|10-year Treasury yield|4.72%|10-year real yield|2.44%|10-year breakeven inflation|2.28%|Investment-grade corporate spread|0.81%|High-yield corporate spread|2.70%@@What moved was the real yield, not breakeven inflation. Money itself got more expensive, and this is not an inflation scare. At 0.81% the investment-grade spread is far too thin to absorb the move in Treasury yields, which supports the author's premise. It is still wider than the 0.53% of October 1997, so it is not a record low.@@2026-08-17 · FRED (DGS30 · DGS10 · DFII10 · T10YIE · BAMLC0A0CM · BAMLH0A0HYM2)

When borrowing costs rise, the businesses hurt first are the ones that spend heavily up front and recover it later through usage fees, which is exactly how a data centre works.
The rent has to rise as much as the funding cost did to break even, and when competition stops that from happening, the difference comes out of profit.

As that report notes, yields were not the only weight on the market that day.
Oil rose too, and the two pushed in the same direction on the arithmetic of data-centre investment.

## What Nvidia can answer on August 26

The rule that higher rates sink tech stocks does not always hold.
Rates were high all through 2026, and tech went to record highs anyway.
A discount rate is only the measuring stick. If earnings grow faster than the stick lengthens, the stick loses.

So the question now is not the direction of yields but the speed of earnings.
Nvidia reports its fiscal 2027 second quarter on August 26, and that number is the speedometer.
Revenue and next-quarter guidance above expectations would be evidence that the sector can carry a heavier stick.
Falling short would undercut the very reason the market has been willing to pay these prices at these yields.

Each House district elects exactly one member.
Winning with 90% and winning with 51% both yield one seat, so where you win matters more than by how much.
Democratic votes are concentrated in cities, which leaves the party with many blowout wins and many narrow losses at the same time.
The same national vote share turns into fewer seats.

Gerrymandering is the practice of bending district lines to amplify that effect for whoever draws them.
G. Elliott Morris calculates that under the current maps Democrats must win the national House vote by 4 points to take the chamber.

The real-economy figure is worse than the headline.
Household loans fell by 460.3 billion yuan and corporate loans by 130 billion yuan, which is 590.3 billion yuan between them.

## The loan growth rate in mid-September

A single month is seasonal. July is when banks that hit their half-year targets ease off.

That rate slipped to 5.1% in July from 5.2% in June, and new lending in the first seven months came to 10.38 trillion yuan against 12.87 trillion a year earlier, a fifth less.
